# Foreclosure Data Hub

> REST API documentation for foreclosure, auction, and property data.

## Foreclosure Data Hub documentation

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs

Build with foreclosure, auction, and property data.

Use the Foreclosure Data Hub REST API to search property feeds, trustee sales, sheriff sales, tax sales, tax delinquency, and early filings. Discover category coverage, retrieve records, and track matching counts.

<Info>API base URL: `https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1`. Documentation hosting does not change your API keys or endpoint URLs.</Info>

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Make your first request" icon="bolt" href="/quickstart">Create an API key and query a small set of listings.</Card>
  <Card title="API reference" icon="code" href="/api-reference/search-properties">Explore parameters, responses, and code examples.</Card>
  <Card title="Sources and coverage" icon="database" href="/api-reference/list-sources">Discover available feeds and supported filters.</Card>
  <Card title="Commercial integrations" icon="building" href="/guides/licensing">Understand internal use and customer-facing integrations.</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Overview

The API uses HTTPS, JSON responses, and an `x-api-key` header. Retail API access is available on eligible Pro and Business subscriptions; Starter does not include API access. Commercial licenses use separate keys and allowances.

## Authentication

Generate a key in [API settings](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/api), then follow the [authentication guide](/authentication).

## Rate limits

Review [rate limits and row allowances](/concepts/rate-limits) before sending requests. API property responses share retail row allowances with CSV and Google Sheets exports.

## Response format

Keep each listing's `source` and `row_id` for reconciliation. See the [response field guide](/concepts/responses).

## Endpoints

- [List sources](/api-reference/list-sources)
- [Search properties](/api-reference/search-properties)
- [Unified search](/api-reference/unified-search)
- [Get source data](/api-reference/single-source-data)
- [Get record counts](/api-reference/record-counts)

## Category endpoints

Choose a [foreclosure data category](/guides/foreclosure-categories), then use its search and counts endpoints. Category searches return normalized records with explicit record units and category-specific fields.

## Preforeclosure search

[Search scheduled-sale preforeclosures](/guides/preforeclosure-search) with `pre_foreclosure=true` and a location filter.

## Errors

See [error handling](/concepts/errors) for invalid parameters, authentication, quota errors, and retries.

---

## Quickstart

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/quickstart

Make your first authenticated request in minutes.

<Steps>
<Step title="Create an API key">
Open [API settings](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/api). Retail API access requires an eligible Pro or Business subscription. For a customer-facing product, use a [commercial license](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/data-licensing).

Store your key in a server-side environment variable:

```bash
export FDH_API_KEY="fdh_ak_your_key_here"
```
</Step>
<Step title="Discover available sources">
```bash
curl --fail-with-body \
  -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources"
```
Use the returned source IDs and coverage metadata. Do not assume a particular feed is available in every county.
</Step>
<Step title="Search a small page of listings">
```bash
curl --fail-with-body \
  -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?mode=unified&state=FL&page_size=5"
```
The response includes `data.records` and pagination in `meta`. Five rows fits the per-response limits of both paid and new trial keys, provided your remaining allowance is sufficient.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>Each new property request, including a retry, can consume rows again. Check the response and quota headers before retrying.</Warning>

Use [category search endpoints](/guides/foreclosure-categories) for trustee sales, sheriff sales, tax sales, tax delinquency, or early filings. For example:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/search?state=SC&page_size=5"
```

Continue with [pagination](/guides/pagination) or [preforeclosure search](/guides/preforeclosure-search).

---

## Authentication

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/authentication

Authenticate requests with your API key.

Pass your API key in the `x-api-key` header on every request. Generate and manage retail keys in [API settings](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/api).

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources"
```

Keep keys in server-side environment variables. Do not put a key in a public repository, browser bundle, or URL query string.

## Retail access

Eligible Pro and Business subscriptions include API access. Starter does not. New Pro and Business trials include **30 total API requests**, at most **10 property rows per response**, and **500 delivered rows shared with CSV and Google Sheets**. Every trial API endpoint counts toward the request cap, including sources and counts.

## Commercial access

Use a commercial license for showing records to your own customers. Manage commercial access in the [license dashboard](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/license). Commercial evaluations and paid licenses have their own call and response limits. See [licensing](/guides/licensing).

Missing or invalid keys return `401`. Inactive subscriptions or ineligible plans return `403`.

---

## Rate limits and allowances

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/concepts/rate-limits

Understand request limits, row delivery, and retry behavior.

## Retail request limits

All retail keys on an account share these limits:

| Endpoint | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Search | 15 requests/minute |
| Source data | 30 requests/minute |
| Counts | 15 requests/minute |
| Sources | 10 requests/minute |
| All endpoints combined | 1,000 requests/hour |
| New trial | 30 requests total |

Category searches share the Search bucket with property search; category counts share the Counts bucket. Source discovery, including category discovery, shares the Sources bucket. Switching categories does not reset or multiply these limits.

Exceeding a rate limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`.

## Retail row allowances

Pro includes **10,000 rows/month**. Business includes **30,000 shared rows/month** and five people. CSV, Google Sheets, and API property responses share the account's row allowance. Unused rows do not roll over.

Paid property responses return at most **100 rows**, defaulting to 25. New trial responses return at most **10 rows**, shared with the trial's **500 delivered rows**. Sources and counts consume requests but do not consume listing rows.

On the first page, an omitted size may be reduced to the remaining balance. Explicit sizes are never silently reduced. A request above your allowance returns `403 EXPORT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` with the remaining rows and reset date; request a smaller count explicitly.

Successful property responses include:

- `X-Export-Quota-Limit`
- `X-Export-Quota-Remaining`
- `X-Export-Quota-Reset` (Unix seconds)

View current usage in [Settings → Subscription](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/settings/subscription).

<Warning>Rows are charged immediately before sending the prepared response. Every new request, including a retry, can consume rows again. If delivery is uncertain, check the result before sending another request.</Warning>

## Commercial limits

Commercial evaluations allow **50 successful calls total over three days**, **10 records per response**, and **10 requests/minute**. They do not reset monthly or convert automatically, and no card is required. Paid commercial licenses use separate monthly call allowances and allow at most 100 records per response. See [commercial licensing](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/data-licensing) for current tiers.

All five category searches use the same retail and commercial allowances. Each returned sale, delinquency, or filing record counts as one delivered row under retail accounting. Category counts and source discovery consume requests but no delivered rows.

---

## Responses and property fields

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/concepts/responses

Read response envelopes, listing identities, and enrichment fields.

Successful responses contain `data` and optional `meta`. Errors contain an `error` message and may include a machine-readable code or quota details.

```json
{"data":{"records":[]},"meta":{"total":0,"page":1,"per_page":5,"total_pages":0}}
```

## Listing identity

Retain `source`, `row_id`, and the response's `X-Request-ID` header for reconciliation and support. These identify listing records, not unique parcels. Grouped search and source-data responses preserve source-specific field names. Use `mode=unified` for consistent fields.

`file_number` is a feed reference when supplied. It may be an asset or trustee reference rather than a court case number. Missing references and unresolved owner names are `null`.

## Sale status

Unified listings include the source's `sale_status` and a normalized `sale_status_group`. Filter by the canonical group with `sale_status` in unified mode. Missing reported statuses can be selected with `sale_status=none`.

## Enrichment

Assessor and public-record enrichment is best effort and runs after ingest. Older listings and some feeds omit these fields. Treat enrichment fields as optional and nullable. Internal processing markers are not returned.

| Unified field | By-source enrichment field | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `building_type` | `enrichment.building_type` | Building profile |
| `build_quality` | `enrichment.build_quality` | Reported quality |
| `num_bedrooms` | `enrichment.bedrooms` | Bedroom count as reported |
| `living_sqft` | `enrichment.living_sqft` | Living area as reported |
| `assessor_year_built` | `enrichment.year_built` | Assessor year built |
| `land_use` | `enrichment.property_type` | Assessor land use |
| `last_sold_price` | `enrichment.last_sold_price` | Last recorded sale price |
| `last_sold_date` | `enrichment.last_sold_date` | Last recorded sale date |
| `mortgage_amount` | `enrichment.loan_amount` | Original recorded loan principal |
| `mortgage_date` | `enrichment.loan_origination_date` | Loan origination date |
| `mortgage_term` | `enrichment.loan_term` | Reported loan term |
| `mortgage_maturity_date` | `enrichment.loan_maturity_date` | Loan maturity date |

Raw enrichment can also include `building_sqft` and `actual_year_built`. Numeric variants such as `zestimate_numeric`, `last_sold_price_numeric`, and `mortgage_amount_numeric` are available in unified responses where populated.

<Note>The raw source column `Mortgage amount due` holds the loan maturity **date**. `enrichment.loan_maturity_date` exposes the same value under a clearer name.</Note>

## Lender identity

`lender_name` is nullable and comes from source mortgage text or explicitly identified parties in notices matched to the property and sale event. It reports the mortgage party in that evidence; it does not independently establish today's loan owner or servicer. Ambiguous or unresolved values are `null`. The source mortgage may differ from the assessor loan represented by `mortgage_amount`.

Raw by-source records include `Lender Name` where captured. Unified responses also include lender names recovered through notice matching.

## Estimated equity

`estimated_equity` is available in unified responses. It is estimated value minus the original recorded loan principal. It ignores principal paid down and secondary liens, can be negative, and is not a payoff figure.


## Category records

Category searches use `data.records` and pagination in `meta`, including `category` and `unit`. They have explicit OpenAPI schemas: `TrusteeSale`, `SheriffSale`, `TaxSale`, `TaxDelinquentProperty`, and `FilingProperty`. Category-specific fields are nullable when no value is supplied. Internal review, capture IDs, and processing metadata are excluded.

Sale records retain the normalized property fields. Tax sales add parcel bundles, tax sale type/status, published bid amounts, source dates, time zone, and expiry. Sheriff sales add authority, legal basis, parcel/auction identifiers, and source expiry. Delinquency and filing records use their own amount, date, party, and identity fields; they do not fabricate sale dates. Read the [category guide](/guides/foreclosure-categories) for counting and reconciliation rules.

---

## Errors and retries

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/concepts/errors

Handle authentication, validation, quota, and service errors.

| Status | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Invalid or missing parameters | Check location filters, source ID, dates, and page size. |
| 401 | Missing or invalid API key | Check the `x-api-key` header and active key. |
| 403 | Plan, license, trial, or row allowance restriction | Check the error code and dashboard usage. |
| 413 | Prepared response exceeds the byte limit | Request fewer rows or narrower filters. |
| 404 | Unknown API endpoint | Verify the endpoint path. Empty queries normally return a successful empty result. |
| 429 | Request rate limit | Respect `Retry-After` before retrying. |
| 500 / 503 | Service failure or temporary unavailability | Retry cautiously with backoff; retain `X-Request-ID` for support. |

```json
{"error":"At least one filter required: county, state, zip, or address"}
```

For `EXPORT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, request fewer rows or wait for the stated reset. Do not repeatedly retry an unchanged oversized request. Each new property request can consume rows again if the previous response was prepared but delivery could not be confirmed.

Contact [support](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/contact) with the request ID and endpoint. Do not send your API key.

New category endpoints return `400` for unknown or repeated scalar parameters, incompatible filters, invalid states/dates, reversed ranges, or unsupported pagination. An unavailable category reader returns `503`; a successful query with no matches returns `200` and an empty result.

---

## Choose a foreclosure data category

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/guides/foreclosure-categories

Choose between trustee sales, sheriff sales, tax sales, tax delinquency, and early filings, with clear date, identity, coverage, and counting rules.

Choose a Foreclosure Data Hub category that matches the records you need. Sale listings, delinquent tax accounts, and recorded filing events represent different stages and use different dates and counting units.

| Category | Search | Counting unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trustee Sales | [Trustee search](/api-reference/trustee-sales/search) | Sale listings |
| Sheriff Sales | [Sheriff search](/api-reference/sheriff-sales/search) | Sale listings |
| Tax Sales | [Tax sale search](/api-reference/tax-sales/search) | Sale lots, potentially containing several parcels |
| Tax Delinquency | [Delinquency search](/api-reference/tax-delinquent/search) | Published property/account records |
| Early Filings | [Filing search](/api-reference/filings/search) | Eligible proceeding and parcel groups |

Each category has `/search` and `/counts` endpoints under `/api/v1`. Searches return `data.records` and `meta`; counts return `data.total`, `data.category`, and `data.unit`. They use the same API keys, rate limits, and applicable row allowances as the existing property endpoints.

## Dates and statuses

Trustee and sheriff filters use sale dates. Trustee searches default to all dates and statuses; `sale_status=trustee-upcoming` selects qualified upcoming sales.

Tax Sales supports `tax_deed`, `redeemable_deed`, and `tax_lien_certificate`. Its default `tax_status=all` includes published available inventory without a scheduled auction. Use `tax_status=upcoming` for qualified upcoming sales. Tax-sale time zones and local sale-day calculations are returned separately. Missing sale dates or minimum bids do not satisfy date or bid ranges.

Tax Delinquency has a `source_as_of` date and collection/expiry timestamps. The published balance can be principal or a delinquent total; read `amount_kind` before comparing amounts. Delinquency alone does not establish a scheduled sale.

Early Filings uses `recorded_from` and `recorded_to` against `record_date`. Filing types include mortgage, HOA, and tax/government candidates. A candidate classification does not establish a completed foreclosure. Recorded grantors and grantees are not automatically current owners. `state` describes the filing jurisdiction; `situs_state` describes the matched property.

## Identity and counting

Retain `source` and `row_id` for every delivered record. These identify category records, not globally unique parcels. Tax lots can bundle parcels. Filings group eligible events by proceeding and parcel; their stable `row_id` can remain the same when a different event represents the group. `event_id`, `proceeding_id`, `parcel_id`, and `event_count` describe the filing result.

Do not add category totals and label the sum unique properties. One property can appear in more than one category or sale event. Counts and pages can change between requests as source inventory changes.

## Coverage and freshness

Use [List sources](/api-reference/list-sources) with a `category` to discover coverage and supported filters. Trustee, sheriff, and tax-sale discovery describes configured coverage, not current inventory or complete county coverage. Delinquency discovery reports published source metadata. Filing discovery includes only sources represented in eligible current inventory.

A valid query with no matching records returns `200` with an empty list and zero total. A reader that cannot establish availability returns `503`. Expired, held, or privacy-suppressed records remain subject to the category's publication rules. An unavailable or missing listing does not imply that a sale completed or a delinquent balance was paid.

## Compatibility

The existing `/properties/search`, `/properties/data`, `/properties/counts`, and unfiltered `/sources` responses retain their behavior. The existing `pre_foreclosure=true` filter still selects scheduled-sale preforeclosures and does not include early filings without a known sale date.

New category searches return normalized records automatically, support browsing without a location filter, and reject unsupported filters. Sale searches accept repeated state, county, ZIP, and address filters. Delinquency and filing filters are scalar. Source IDs in category discovery describe that category; they are not automatically valid inputs to the legacy `/properties/data` endpoint. Only filing search currently accepts a category `source` filter.

---

## Search preforeclosures

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/guides/preforeclosure-search

Find listings with scheduled upcoming sales.

Set `pre_foreclosure=true` (or `1`) and include a location filter: `county`, `state`, `zip`, or `address`.

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?mode=unified&state=FL&pre_foreclosure=true&page_size=5"
```

This matches the dashboard filter: sale date today or later in UTC, excluding REO-only feeds and REO asset types. Listings without a known sale date, including early-stage defaults, are excluded.

`false` and `0` disable the filter. Other values return `400`.

In unified mode, `sale_days` adds minimum lead time of 1–365 days. It combines with `sale_date_start` and `sale_date_end`. On its own, `sale_days` retains listings without a parsed date; combining it with `pre_foreclosure=true` excludes those undated listings.

Use `sale_status` to narrow canonical status groups in unified mode. Scheduled sale dates can change; check the record's latest status and source evidence before acting on a listing.

For records before a known sale date, use [Early Filings](/api-reference/filings/search). For published overdue property taxes, use [Tax Delinquency](/api-reference/tax-delinquent/search). These categories have separate date and counting semantics.

---

## Pagination and filtering

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/guides/pagination

Retrieve bounded pages without exhausting your allowance.

| Mode | Page | Page size | Response rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category search | `page` | `page_size` | `data.records` |
| Unified search | `page` | `page_size` | `data.records` |
| Single source | `page` | `per_page` | `data` |
| Grouped search | No page parameter | `limit` | `data.results[].records` |

Page numbering starts at 1. Use `meta.total_pages` to stop paginated requests. Grouped search applies one total row budget across all source groups; later groups may have a count and no rows. Use unified search or single-source data to paginate.

Retail paid responses allow up to 100 rows, defaulting to 25; new trials allow up to 10. Use a smaller explicit size when your remaining allowance is low. Commercial response limits depend on license status.

Legacy property search and category sale searches accept repeated location parameters, such as `county=Cook&county=Lake`. Legacy property search requires at least one location filter. New category searches allow paginated browsing without a location filter; delinquency and filing filters cannot be repeated. Source-data filters apply only when supported by the chosen source; discover support with [List sources](/api-reference/list-sources).

The `limit` alias can also bound paginated requests. If you supply it together with `page_size` or `per_page`, use matching values; conflicting limits return `400`.


Category searches reject unknown parameters and repeated scalar values. `page` is limited to 100,000. Tax delinquency also limits starting offsets to 500,000, including the second block in pages larger than 50 rows. Narrow filters for deeper result sets. Keep the same explicit page size while paging; inventory changes can still move records between pages.

Category `/counts` endpoints use the search filters but reject `page`, `page_size`, and `limit`. They consume requests without consuming delivered rows.

---

## Commercial integrations

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/guides/licensing

Choose access for internal workflows or customer-facing products.

Retail Pro and Business subscriptions support internal use. To show records to your own customers, use [commercial data licensing](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/data-licensing).

Commercial keys use the same API endpoints and `x-api-key` header, with separate monthly call allowances. A commercial evaluation includes 50 successful calls over three days, at most 10 records per response, and 10 requests/minute. It does not convert automatically.

Review current tiers and license terms on the [licensing page](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/data-licensing), and manage access in the [license dashboard](https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/dashboard/license).

## List sources

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/list-sources

Discover available feeds, coverage, and supported filters.

List all available data sources with their coverage and supported filters. coverage is one of national (all US states), regional (a subset of states), state (one state), or county (one county). states lists the USPS codes covered; it is null for national feeds and for regional feeds whose footprint varies - query /v1/properties/data with the state filter to enumerate those.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `category` | Optional: `trustee-sales`, `sheriff-sales`, `tax-sales`, `tax-delinquent`, or `filings`. Omit for the original property feed catalog. |

When using `category`, supply it once and do not add other parameters. The response remains a `data` array. Category entries add `category`, `coverage_basis`, and supported filter names. Some include county metadata or source dates.

- `configured`: The source/category is configured for these states or counties. This does not promise current inventory or complete coverage.
- `published`: Delinquency source metadata, including `available` and source/capture/expiry dates when supplied.
- `current_inventory`: Filing sources represented by currently eligible property records.

Tax and sheriff sales each expose an aggregate inventory ID (`tax_sales` and `sheriff_sales`). Trustee feeds retain their numbered IDs. Delinquency and filings use their source keys. These category IDs do not expand the legacy `/properties/data` source catalog.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources?category=tax-sales"
```

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories) before interpreting coverage or totals.

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -H "x-api-key: fdh_ak_your_key_here" \
  https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources
```

```javascript JavaScript
const res = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": "fdh_ak_your_key_here" } }
);
const data = await res.json();
```

```python Python
import requests

res = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sources",
    headers={"x-api-key": "fdh_ak_your_key_here"}
)
data = res.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response shape

Illustrative response; `...` represents omitted fields or records.

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "feed-01",
      "name": "Data Feed 01",
      "coverage": "regional",
      "states": ["AL", "AZ", "CA", "..."],
      "filters": { "county": true, "state": true, "sale_date": true, "owner_name": true, "est_value": true }
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

See [response fields](/concepts/responses), [quotas](/concepts/rate-limits), and [error handling](/concepts/errors).

## Search properties

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/search-properties

Search listings across sources with grouped or unified responses.

Search across all data sources simultaneously. Paid retail requests return up to 100 rows total across all source groups; new trials return up to 10. Groups after the limit contain counts and empty records. At least one location filter (county, state, zip, or address) is required.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | No | Total listing rows across all groups: 1–100 paid or 1–10 during a new trial. Defaults to 25 when paid or 10 during a new trial. Choose a value within your remaining allowance. |
| `mode` | string | No | Use unified for one records array with consistent field names, including source, row_id, nullable owner_first_name / owner_last_name, and file_number where supplied. The default groups source-specific records by feed. |
| `county` | string | No | County name filter. Can specify multiple (e.g., county=Cook&county=Lake). |
| `state` | string | No | State name or abbreviation. Can specify multiple. |
| `zip` | string | No | Zip code filter. Can specify multiple. |
| `address` | string | No | Property address filter (partial match). Can specify multiple. |
| `pre_foreclosure` | boolean | No | Set true or 1 for scheduled-sale preforeclosures: sale date today or later (UTC), excluding REO-only feeds and REO asset types. Matches the dashboard filter. Listings without a known sale date, including early-stage defaults, are excluded. false or 0 disables the filter (default); other values return 400. A location filter is still required. |
| `sale_date_start` | date | No | Filter by sale date start (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `sale_date_end` | date | No | Filter by sale date end (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `owner_name` | string | No | Owner name filter (partial match on first or last name). Only applied to sources that expose owner fields. |
| `est_value_min` | number | No | Minimum estimated value (Market Valuation). Only applied to sources with an estimated value field. |
| `est_value_max` | number | No | Maximum estimated value (Market Valuation). Only applied to sources with an estimated value field. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -H "x-api-key: fdh_ak_..." \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?state=FL&county=Miami-Dade"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const params = new URLSearchParams({
  state: "FL",
  county: "Miami-Dade",
});

const res = await fetch(
  `https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?${params}`,
  { headers: { "x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..." } }
);
const data = await res.json();
```

```python Python
import requests

res = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search",
    headers={"x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..."},
    params={"state": "FL", "county": "Miami-Dade"}
)
data = res.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response shape

Illustrative response; `...` represents omitted fields or records.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "results": [
      {
        "source": "feed-01",
        "source_name": "Data Feed 01",
        "records": [ { "source": "feed-01", "row_id": "listing-record-id", ... }, ... ],
        "count": 45,
        "has_more": false
      },
      ...
    ]
  },
  "meta": { "total": 312 }
}
```

See [response fields](/concepts/responses), [quotas](/concepts/rate-limits), and [error handling](/concepts/errors).

---

## Unified search

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/unified-search

Search with mode=unified to get normalized, paginated results across all sources in a single flat list. Each record includes standardized fields (address, city, state, zip, county, sale_date, bid_amount, owner name, etc.) with a source field indicating origin.

Search with mode=unified to get normalized, paginated results across all sources in a single flat list. Each record includes standardized fields (address, city, state, zip, county, sale_date, bid_amount, owner name, etc.) with a source field indicating origin.

Use the search endpoint with `mode=unified`. At least one location filter is required.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string | Yes | Set to "unified" to enable unified mode. |
| `county` | string | No | County name filter. Can specify multiple. |
| `state` | string | No | State name or abbreviation. Can specify multiple. |
| `zip` | string | No | Zip code filter. Can specify multiple. |
| `address` | string | No | Property address filter (partial match). Can specify multiple. |
| `pre_foreclosure` | boolean | No | Set true or 1 for scheduled-sale preforeclosures: sale date today or later (UTC), excluding REO-only feeds and REO asset types. Matches the dashboard filter. Listings without a known sale date, including early-stage defaults, are excluded. false or 0 disables the filter (default); other values return 400. A location filter is still required. |
| `sale_date_start` | date | No | Filter by sale date start (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `sale_date_end` | date | No | Filter by sale date end (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `sale_days` | integer | No | Minimum lead time: sale_date_parsed must be later than today + N days (integer 1-365, unbounded above). ANDs with sale_date_start/sale_date_end. Listings without a parsed sale date stay included — an unscheduled sale cannot violate the bound. Unified mode only. |
| `sale_status` | string | No | Canonical sale-status group: active, coming-soon, for-sale, postponed, cancelled, price-reduced, back-to-bank, new-listing, sold, mortgage-foreclosure, outbid, preview, pending, hard-to-sell, nos, vacant-lot, sale-held, none. Groups merge clearly-equivalent feed statuses — e.g. cancelled covers Cancelled/WITHDRAWN/Sale Invalid, sold covers Sold/Completed/3rd-party variants, postponed covers postpone*/On Hold. none matches listings with no reported status. Unified mode only. |
| `owner_name` | string | No | Owner name filter (partial match on first or last name). |
| `est_value_min` | number | No | Minimum estimated value (Market Valuation). Uses the unified zestimate_numeric column. |
| `est_value_max` | number | No | Maximum estimated value (Market Valuation). Uses the unified zestimate_numeric column. |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number (default: 1). |
| `page_size` | integer | No | Results per page, 1–100 for paid keys or 1–10 for new trials. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 during a trial. Your remaining allowance may lower an omitted first-page size. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -H "x-api-key: fdh_ak_..." \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?mode=unified&state=FL&pre_foreclosure=true&page=1&page_size=25"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const params = new URLSearchParams({
  mode: "unified",
  state: "FL",
  pre_foreclosure: "true",
  page: "1",
  page_size: "25",
});

const res = await fetch(
  `https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search?${params}`,
  { headers: { "x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..." } }
);
const data = await res.json();
```

```python Python
import requests

res = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/search",
    headers={"x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..."},
    params={
        "mode": "unified",
        "state": "FL",
        "pre_foreclosure": "true",
        "page": 1,
        "page_size": 25
    }
)
data = res.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response shape

Illustrative response; `...` represents omitted fields or records.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "records": [
      {
        "source": "feed-01",
        "address": "123 Main St",
        "city": "Miami",
        "state": "FL",
        "zip": "33101",
        "county": "Miami-Dade",
        "sale_date": "2026-04-15",
        "sale_status": "Postponed",
        "sale_status_group": "postponed",
        "bid_amount": "250000",
        "owner_first_name": "John",
        "owner_last_name": "Doe",
        ...
      },
      ...
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "total": 1250,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 25,
    "total_pages": 50
  }
}
```

See [response fields](/concepts/responses), [quotas](/concepts/rate-limits), and [error handling](/concepts/errors).

## Get source data

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/single-source-data

Retrieve a paginated set of listings from one source.

Fetch paginated data from a single source. Max 100 records per page when paid, or 10 during a new trial. Defaults to 25 when paid or 10 during a new trial.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | string | Yes | Data source ID (from /v1/sources). |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number (default: 1). |
| `per_page` | integer | No | Results per page, 1–100 paid or 1–10 during a new trial. Defaults to 25 when paid or 10 during a new trial. |
| `start_date` | date | No | Filter by date added start (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | date | No | Filter by date added end (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `county` | string | No | County name filter. |
| `state` | string | No | State name or abbreviation. |
| `owner_name` | string | No | Owner name filter (partial match on first or last name). Only applied when the source exposes owner fields. |
| `est_value_min` | number | No | Minimum estimated value (Market Valuation). Only applied when the source exposes an estimated value field. |
| `est_value_max` | number | No | Maximum estimated value (Market Valuation). Only applied when the source exposes an estimated value field. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -H "x-api-key: fdh_ak_..." \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/data?source=feed-01&state=TX&per_page=25"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const params = new URLSearchParams({
  source: "feed-01",
  state: "TX",
  per_page: "25",
});

const res = await fetch(
  `https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/data?${params}`,
  { headers: { "x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..." } }
);
const data = await res.json();
```

```python Python
import requests

res = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/properties/data",
    headers={"x-api-key": "fdh_ak_..."},
    params={"source": "feed-01", "state": "TX", "per_page": 25}
)
data = res.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response shape

Illustrative response; `...` represents omitted fields or records.

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "Address": "123 Main St", "County": "Harris", ... },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": 1250,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 25,
    "total_pages": 50
  }
}
```

See [response fields](/concepts/responses), [quotas](/concepts/rate-limits), and [error handling](/concepts/errors).

## Search trustee sales

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/trustee-sales/search

Find trustee sales with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Trustee Sales returns the classified dashboard inventory. Omit sale_status for all dates and statuses; use trustee-upcoming for qualified upcoming sales. The nullable trustee_status, trustee_today and trustee_upcoming fields are populated when supplied by the selected status projection.

Results are normalized automatically in `data.records`. No `mode=unified` or location filter is required. Each returned row consumes the applicable delivered-row allowance.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `county` | Partial county name. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `zip` | Property ZIP prefix. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `address` | Partial property address. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `sale_date_start` | Inclusive sale date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_date_end` | Inclusive sale date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_days` | Minimum sale lead time, 1 to 365 days. Tax sales require a known date and use local sale days. Trustee and sheriff searches retain undated rows unless another date filter excludes them. |
| `sale_status` | Canonical status group, including trustee-upcoming, trustee-active and trustee-unconfirmed. Omit for all trustee statuses and dates. |
| `owner_name` | Partial published owner name. |
| `est_value_min` | Minimum estimated value. |
| `est_value_max` | Maximum estimated value. |
| `pre_foreclosure` | Scheduled-sale preforeclosure filter; does not search early filing events. |
| `page` | Page number, starting at 1. Keep page_size fixed while paging. |
| `page_size` | Rows per page: 1 to 100 paid, 1 to 10 trial. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 trial. An omitted first-page size may shrink to the remaining allowance. |
| `limit` | Alias for page_size; values must match when both are supplied. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/search?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming&page_size=5"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/search?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming&page_size=5",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/search?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming&page_size=5",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

The OpenAPI response panel includes a synthetic record example and an empty result. Example identities and property details are illustrative.

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "records": []
  },
  "meta": {
    "category": "trustee-sales",
    "unit": "sale_listings",
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total_pages": 0
  }
}
```

Records follow the `TrusteeSale` schema in the OpenAPI reference. Retain `source` and `row_id` for reconciliation. Use [matching counts](/api-reference/trustee-sales/counts) to check result size. Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).

---

## Count trustee sales

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/trustee-sales/counts

Count trustee sales with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Use Foreclosure Data Hub to count matching trustee sales before retrieving a page. Counts use the search filters and eligibility rules, with a `sale_listings` unit.

This endpoint consumes an API request but no delivered rows. Its total counts category records, not distinct properties across categories. Pagination parameters are not accepted.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `county` | Partial county name. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `zip` | Property ZIP prefix. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `address` | Partial property address. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `sale_date_start` | Inclusive sale date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_date_end` | Inclusive sale date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_days` | Minimum sale lead time, 1 to 365 days. Tax sales require a known date and use local sale days. Trustee and sheriff searches retain undated rows unless another date filter excludes them. |
| `sale_status` | Canonical status group, including trustee-upcoming, trustee-active and trustee-unconfirmed. Omit for all trustee statuses and dates. |
| `owner_name` | Partial published owner name. |
| `est_value_min` | Minimum estimated value. |
| `est_value_max` | Maximum estimated value. |
| `pre_foreclosure` | Scheduled-sale preforeclosure filter; does not search early filing events. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/counts?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming"
```

```javascript JavaScript
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/counts?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python

import requests

    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/trustee-sales/counts?state=CA&sale_status=trustee-upcoming",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json

  "data": {
    "category": "trustee-sales",
    "unit": "sale_listings",
    "total": 0
  }
}
```

`total` matches the search total for identical filters against the same inventory. Retrieve [matching records](/api-reference/trustee-sales/search). Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).

## Search sheriff sales

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/sheriff-sales/search

Find sheriff sales with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Sheriff Sales returns qualified sheriff-administered mortgage sale listings, preserving authority and legal basis. Customer-facing scheduled statuses are returned as Scheduled. Owner, valuation and generic sale-status filters are unsupported.

Results are normalized automatically in `data.records`. No `mode=unified` or location filter is required. Each returned row consumes the applicable delivered-row allowance.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `county` | Partial county name. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `zip` | Property ZIP prefix. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `address` | Partial property address. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `sale_date_start` | Inclusive sale date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_date_end` | Inclusive sale date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_days` | Minimum sale lead time, 1 to 365 days. Tax sales require a known date and use local sale days. Trustee and sheriff searches retain undated rows unless another date filter excludes them. |
| `q` | Search parcel, case, writ, or auction identifiers. |
| `page` | Page number, starting at 1. Keep page_size fixed while paging. |
| `page_size` | Rows per page: 1 to 100 paid, 1 to 10 trial. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 trial. An omitted first-page size may shrink to the remaining allowance. |
| `limit` | Alias for page_size; values must match when both are supplied. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>


```javascript JavaScript
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python

import requests

    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/sheriff-sales/search?state=PA&county=Philadelphia&page_size=5",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Search tax sales

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/tax-sales/search

Find tax sales with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Tax Sales includes tax deeds, redeemable deeds, tax lien certificates and published available inventory. A row is a sale lot and may contain several parcels. The default tax_status=all includes undated available records. Date filters exclude undated records; missing bids do not match bid ranges.

Results are normalized automatically in `data.records`. No `mode=unified` or location filter is required. Each returned row consumes the applicable delivered-row allowance.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `county` | Partial county name. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `zip` | Property ZIP prefix. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `address` | Partial property address. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `sale_date_start` | Inclusive sale date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_date_end` | Inclusive sale date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_days` | Minimum sale lead time, 1 to 365 days. Tax sales require a known date and use local sale days. Trustee and sheriff searches retain undated rows unless another date filter excludes them. |
| `owner_name` | Partial published owner name. |
| `tax_sale_type` | Type of tax sale or interest. |
| `tax_status` | all includes undated available inventory; upcoming selects qualified upcoming sales. |
| `minimum_bid_min` | Minimum published minimum bid; unknown bids do not match. |
| `minimum_bid_max` | Maximum published minimum bid; unknown bids do not match. |
| `q` | Search parcel and case identifiers. |
| `page` | Page number, starting at 1. Keep page_size fixed while paging. |
| `page_size` | Rows per page: 1 to 100 paid, 1 to 10 trial. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 trial. An omitted first-page size may shrink to the remaining allowance. |
| `limit` | Alias for page_size; values must match when both are supplied. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/search?state=SC&tax_status=all&page_size=5"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/search?state=SC&tax_status=all&page_size=5",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/search?state=SC&tax_status=all&page_size=5",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

The OpenAPI response panel includes a synthetic record example and an empty result. Example identities and property details are illustrative.

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "records": []
  },
  "meta": {
    "category": "tax-sales",
    "unit": "sale_lots",
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total_pages": 0
  }
}
```

Records follow the `TaxSale` schema in the OpenAPI reference. Retain `source` and `row_id` for reconciliation. Use [matching counts](/api-reference/tax-sales/counts) to check result size. Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).

---

## Count tax sales

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/tax-sales/counts

Count tax sales with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Use Foreclosure Data Hub to count matching tax sales before retrieving a page. Counts use the search filters and eligibility rules, with a `sale_lots` unit.

This endpoint consumes an API request but no delivered rows. Its total counts category records, not distinct properties across categories. Pagination parameters are not accepted.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `county` | Partial county name. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `zip` | Property ZIP prefix. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `address` | Partial property address. Repeat for multiple values, at most 50. |
| `sale_date_start` | Inclusive sale date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_date_end` | Inclusive sale date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `sale_days` | Minimum sale lead time, 1 to 365 days. Tax sales require a known date and use local sale days. Trustee and sheriff searches retain undated rows unless another date filter excludes them. |
| `owner_name` | Partial published owner name. |
| `tax_sale_type` | Type of tax sale or interest. |
| `tax_status` | all includes undated available inventory; upcoming selects qualified upcoming sales. |
| `minimum_bid_min` | Minimum published minimum bid; unknown bids do not match. |
| `minimum_bid_max` | Maximum published minimum bid; unknown bids do not match. |
| `q` | Search parcel and case identifiers. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/counts?state=SC&tax_status=all"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/counts?state=SC&tax_status=all",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-sales/counts?state=SC&tax_status=all",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "category": "tax-sales",
    "unit": "sale_lots",
    "total": 0
  }
}
```

`total` matches the search total for identical filters against the same inventory. Retrieve [matching records](/api-reference/tax-sales/search). Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).

---

## Search tax delinquency

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/tax-delinquent/search

Find tax delinquency with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Tax Delinquency returns published delinquent property/account records. Read amount_kind with reported_balance; published_total is separate and nullable. These records do not imply an auction date. Starting offsets are limited to 500,000, including the second block of pages larger than 50 rows.

Results are normalized automatically in `data.records`. No `mode=unified` or location filter is required. Each returned row consumes the applicable delivered-row allowance.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | US state name or abbreviation. |
| `county` | Exact county name, case-insensitive. |
| `field` | Delinquency field searched by q. Parcel also searches account aliases. |
| `q` | Search the selected field; parcel also searches account aliases. |
| `minimum` | Minimum reported delinquent balance. |
| `maximum` | Maximum reported delinquent balance. |
| `page` | Page number, starting at 1. Keep page_size fixed while paging. |
| `page_size` | Rows per page: 1 to 100 paid, 1 to 10 trial. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 trial. An omitted first-page size may shrink to the remaining allowance. |
| `limit` | Alias for page_size; values must match when both are supplied. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-delinquent/search?state=TX&field=owner&q=Example&page_size=5"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-delinquent/search?state=TX&field=owner&q=Example&page_size=5",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/tax-delinquent/search?state=TX&field=owner&q=Example&page_size=5",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

The OpenAPI response panel includes a synthetic record example and an empty result. Example identities and property details are illustrative.

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "records": []
  },
  "meta": {
    "category": "tax-delinquent",
    "unit": "properties",
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total_pages": 0
  }
}
```

Records follow the `TaxDelinquentProperty` schema in the OpenAPI reference. Retain `source` and `row_id` for reconciliation. Use [matching counts](/api-reference/tax-delinquent/counts) to check result size. Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).

## Search early filings

Source: https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/docs/api-reference/filings/search

Find early filings with category-specific filters, explicit record units, and the API keys and allowances shared across Foreclosure Data Hub.

Early Filings returns eligible matched properties grouped by proceeding and parcel. It includes recording dates, document references, classifications and recorded parties. state filters filing jurisdiction; situs_state describes the matched property. Internal review and unresolved-match data are excluded.

Results are normalized automatically in `data.records`. No `mode=unified` or location filter is required. Each returned row consumes the applicable delivered-row allowance.

## Parameters

Unknown parameters and repeated scalar parameters return `400`. Date and numeric ranges must run from lower to higher values.

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | Filing jurisdiction as a US state name or abbreviation. |
| `county` | Partial county name or qualified county key such as FL:Duval. |
| `source` | Filing source ID from /sources?category=filings. |
| `q` | Search instrument, case, address, legal text, and recorded parties. |
| `recorded_from` | Inclusive recording date start, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `recorded_to` | Inclusive recording date end, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `event_type` | Recorded event type; results remain eligible property groups. |
| `filing_kind` | Filing classification; a candidate does not establish a completed foreclosure. |
| `has_case` | Require a reported case number. |
| `page` | Page number, starting at 1. Keep page_size fixed while paging. |
| `page_size` | Rows per page: 1 to 100 paid, 1 to 10 trial. Defaults to 25 paid or 10 trial. An omitted first-page size may shrink to the remaining allowance. |
| `limit` | Alias for page_size; values must match when both are supplied. |

## Examples

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl --fail-with-body -H "x-api-key: $FDH_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/filings/search?state=FL&recorded_from=2026-10-01&page_size=5"
```

```javascript JavaScript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/filings/search?state=FL&recorded_from=2026-10-01&page_size=5",
  { headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.FDH_API_KEY } }
);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`API request failed: ${response.status}`);
const result = await response.json();
```

```python Python
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://www.foreclosuredatahub.com/api/v1/filings/search?state=FL&recorded_from=2026-10-01&page_size=5",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["FDH_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=60,
)
response.raise_for_status()
result = response.json()
```

</CodeGroup>

## Response

The OpenAPI response panel includes a synthetic record example and an empty result. Example identities and property details are illustrative.

A query can succeed with no matching records. This valid empty example does not indicate unavailable inventory:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "records": []
  },
  "meta": {
    "category": "filings",
    "unit": "proceeding_parcels",
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 5,
    "total_pages": 0
  }
}
```

Records follow the `FilingProperty` schema in the OpenAPI reference. Retain `source` and `row_id` for reconciliation. Use [matching counts](/api-reference/filings/counts) to check result size. Inventory can change between requests. When the reader reports unavailable data, the API returns `503` instead of a successful empty result.

See [category semantics](/guides/foreclosure-categories), [source discovery](/api-reference/list-sources), [pagination](/guides/pagination), and [allowances](/concepts/rate-limits).
